entries.sense_en: a person who makes and sells things made of gold

synonyms.nuance: Broader: works with any precious stones and metals, and often sells the finished pieces.
Same craft, but the metal is silver, not gold.

entries.sense_en: to manage well in life; to make progress and be comfortable

synonyms.nuance: Only just manage; getting on is more hopeful and successful.
synonyms.example: We can get by on his pay.

synonyms.nuance: Stresses earning money, not general progress.
synonyms.example: He makes a living selling brooms.

entries.sense_en: clever at getting what you want, often by tricking people

synonyms.nuance: Very close; stresses a sly, secret plan.
Less intense; suggests quiet, secretive trickery.
Literary; clever at avoiding traps and getting out of trouble.

entries.sense_en: to suddenly want to do or have something

synonyms.nuance: Modern and neutral; no sense of a sudden whim.
Also a sudden liking, but usually for a person or thing.
synonyms.example: She took a fancy to the ring.

entries.modern: "I have a fancy to eat it" → "I feel like eating it"

entries.sense_en: so strange and wonderful that it fills you with awe

synonyms.nuance: Common and general; means excellent as well as amazing.
Suggests something that seems to break the laws of nature.

entries.sense_en: a long metal rod that holds meat over a fire while it cooks

synonyms.nuance: A short stick for small pieces of food; a spit is turned over a big fire.
A modern machine that turns meat on a spit.

entries.tip_ko: 침을 뱉다(spit)와 철자가 같지만 여기서는 '꼬치' 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: a very small piece of food

synonyms.nuance: A mouthful; can also be the act of biting.
Leftover piece, often not wanted.
A tiny dry piece, mostly of bread or cake.

entries.sense_en: ate all of something

synonyms.nuance: Eat fast and hungrily; more vivid than consume.
Everyday phrase for finishing the food.

entries.sense_en: secretly working together with someone, usually for a bad purpose

synonyms.nuance: Informal; secret partnership in something dishonest.
Neutral; open and formal cooperation, not always bad.

entries.sense_en: feeling unhappy because someone else has what you want

synonyms.nuance: Often about fear of losing what you have; envious is about wanting what others have.
Literary; strongly wanting another person's property.

entries.tip_ko: jealous는 '뺏길까 봐 질투', envious는 '남의 것이 부러움'입니다.

entries.sense_en: to allow something to happen; to let

synonyms.nuance: Modern, neutral word for giving permission.
synonyms.example: Do not allow them to stay.

synonyms.nuance: More formal; often about official permission.

entries.modern: "suffer them to stay" → "allow them to stay"

entries.sense_en: happened to come to someone as their share or fate

synonyms.nuance: Simple; the thing simply reaches the person.
Literary; usually something that happens by fate, often bad.

entries.sense_en: happen; take place

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; "come to pass" sounds old and grand.
More formal and used in writing.

entries.modern: "how it had come to pass" → "how it had happened"

entries.sense_en: a man who hunts wild animals for a living or for sport

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for anyone who hunts.
Looks after the game on an estate and stops poachers.

entries.sense_en: to look after a child until they are grown

synonyms.nuance: Common in American English; the same meaning.
Formal; also used for animals.

entries.sense_en: the time when a young person learns a trade from an expert

synonyms.nuance: General; any teaching, not always under one master.
Modern, short, often unpaid, in an office job.

entries.sense_en: a small group of wild birds flying together

synonyms.nuance: Any group of birds; covey is smaller and for game birds.
A group of birds flying together.

entries.sense_en: talked together to decide what to do

synonyms.nuance: Ask advice from someone; here the two talk to each other.
Formal; talk together about a decision.

entries.sense_en: told or ordered someone to do something

synonyms.nuance: Modern; a plain command.
Weaker, without the sense of authority.

entries.sense_en: doing; how well or badly someone is getting on

synonyms.nuance: Everyday; "how is he doing".
British; making progress in life.

entries.modern: "how his brother is faring" → "how his brother is doing"

entries.sense_en: saying goodbye

synonyms.nuance: Plain and modern.
synonyms.example: We said goodbye at the gate.

synonyms.nuance: Formal or literary; go separate ways.

entries.sense_en: a thick group of bushes and small trees

synonyms.nuance: Low plants under trees, not a separate patch.
A small group of trees, more open than a thicket.

entries.sense_en: feel able to do something, usually something unkind

synonyms.nuance: Very close; usually with something hard or unpleasant.
synonyms.example: I could not bring myself to say it.

synonyms.nuance: Common in negatives.
synonyms.example: She didn't have the heart to refuse.

entries.sense_en: walked with long, confident steps

synonyms.nuance: Steady steps like a soldier; strode is proud and free.
Stiff, angry, or hunting steps.
Slow, heavy, tired steps.

entries.sense_en: the long thick hair on a lion's or horse's neck

synonyms.nuance: The ridge on a bird's head or a horse's neck; not long hair.
Short soft hair covering an animal's whole body, not one long patch.

entries.sense_en: listen! (an old way to call for attention)

synonyms.nuance: Modern and neutral.
A little formal; asks for attention before a request.

entries.sense_en: made less strong; satisfied

synonyms.nuance: Common; fills a need such as hunger or thirst.
Calms an angry or upset person.
Calms someone by giving them something.

entries.sense_en: farm birds such as hens, kept for meat and eggs

synonyms.nuance: Old-fashioned; often a single bird such as a hen.
Only one kind of bird; poultry covers all.

entries.headword: there is nothing else for it
entries.sense_en: there is no other choice

synonyms.nuance: Direct and modern.
Formal.

entries.sense_en: thin black cloth used as a sign of mourning

synonyms.nuance: Modern spelling of the same fabric.
Cloth that covers or wraps the dead; not a hanging.

entries.sense_en: to have enough room or a place for someone

synonyms.nuance: Give someone or something a place to live.
Informal; give a bed for a night.

entries.tip_ko: 철자에 c와 m이 둘씩 있습니다: ac-com-mo-date.

entries.sense_en: ate quickly and completely

synonyms.nuance: Informal; fast and greedy.
Informal; eat very fast.
Neutral; eat or use up.

entries.sense_en: destroys everything in a place

synonyms.nuance: Very strong damage; also used for feelings.
Violent and widespread damage.

entries.sense_en: strong, healthy and full of energy

synonyms.nuance: Strong and healthy, but stresses toughness, not activity.
Full of active energy.

entries.sense_en: defeats and gets control of an enemy

synonyms.nuance: Win against someone once; conquer suggests gaining control.
Also used for problems and fears.
Literary; a total defeat.

entries.sense_en: words carved or written on a surface

synonyms.nuance: The cut lines or words themselves.
Words under a picture; not carved.

entries.sense_en: to hold and use a weapon or tool with skill

synonyms.nuance: To wave a weapon to show it; wield means to use it.
General; use or control by hand.

entries.tip_ko: ie는 긴 [이-] 소리로, wild[와일드]와 다르게 [위-일드]처럼 읽습니다.

entries.sense_en: the strip of floor at a doorway

synonyms.nuance: The step outside the door.
The whole opening, not just the floor.

entries.sense_en: a high officer at a royal court

synonyms.nuance: A servant who manages a great household.
Leads soldiers; a marshal here is a court officer.

entries.sense_en: a person who serves or attends a king or queen at court

synonyms.nuance: Any person who waits on someone.
Person of high birth, not always at court.

entries.sense_en: noticed; became aware of

synonyms.nuance: Everyday; simply see something.
Informal; see something suddenly.
Formal; see something hard to see.

entries.sense_en: to die or be harmed because one cannot get air

synonyms.nuance: Blocked in the throat, often by food or smoke.
Cover something so no air gets in.

entries.sense_en: stepped on something heavily so it is crushed

synonyms.nuance: One firm hit with the foot.
Just walk on; less rough.
Press flat by any weight.

entries.sense_en: hit hard with a weapon

synonyms.nuance: Modern and general.
Cut with a swinging motion.

entries.sense_en: very great pain of body or mind

synonyms.nuance: Strong pain, often physical.
Milder; worry or suffering.
Long and cruel suffering.

entries.sense_en: saved from danger

synonyms.nuance: Common; save someone from danger.
Most general and everyday.
Let go from a trap or captivity.

entries.sense_en: a small metal fastener on a necklace or belt

synonyms.nuance: A fastener for a belt or strap.
Any small fastener that snaps shut.

entries.sense_en: became conscious again after fainting

synonyms.nuance: British; wake up after fainting.
Formal and medical.

entries.sense_en: became brave enough to act

synonyms.nuance: Informal; make an effort to be brave.
synonyms.example: He plucked up courage to knock.

synonyms.nuance: Prepare to do something frightening.

entries.sense_en: cut roughly into pieces

synonyms.nuance: Cut with several hard blows.
Cut with long, swinging strokes.

entries.sense_en: to control one's strong feelings

synonyms.nuance: Stop oneself from acting on a strong urge.
Keep feelings inside.

entries.sense_en: to agree to something

synonyms.nuance: Everyday and general.
Say that something is good; consent only allows it.
Give permission from a position of power.

entries.sense_en: a large hairy bee that hums loudly

synonyms.nuance: Modern name of the same insect.
Thin, yellow, and stings more easily.

entries.sense_en: begged someone eagerly

synonyms.nuance: Everyday; often with a feeling of need.
Formal; emotional begging.
Ask with strong feeling, often to a judge or king.

entries.sense_en: sad in a quiet, thoughtful way

synonyms.nuance: Dark and hopeless.
Sad with a soft longing for what is gone.
Deep and clear sadness.

entries.sense_en: to hold a marriage with a formal ceremony

synonyms.nuance: Enjoy an event, usually with a party.
Say the ceremony as the priest does.

entries.tip_ko: solemn[살럼]은 끝의 n이 묵음이지만, solemnize에서는 n을 발음합니다.

entries.sense_en: money risked on whether something is true or will happen

synonyms.nuance: Everyday and shorter.
Risk on a chance, often a bigger risk.

entries.sense_en: a small hut where a guard stands

synonyms.nuance: A larger building where guards stay.
A place to watch from.

entries.sense_en: a joke; something not serious

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word.
A trick played on someone.

entries.modern: "did not understand a jest" → "did not get the joke"

entries.sense_en: officially called someone to come

synonyms.nuance: Neutral; ask someone to come.
Plain word; less official.

entries.sense_en: sweet food such as candy and cakes

synonyms.nuance: British word for candy.
American word; smaller sweet items.
Baked food from dough; not always sweet.

entries.sense_en: small sweets that have a hard sugar coating

synonyms.nuance: French-style sweet; usually with a soft center.
Old word for a small sugar sweet.

entries.sense_en: drunk; affected by alcohol

synonyms.nuance: Everyday and direct.
Slightly drunk, cheerful.
Very formal for drunk.

entries.sense_en: with a sideways look showing doubt or dislike

synonyms.nuance: Only the direction, without doubt or disapproval.
Says the feeling but not the look.

entries.sense_en: walked unsteadily, as if about to fall

synonyms.nuance: Same idea; often from injury or weight.
Almost fell by catching the foot.
Moved slowly from side to side.

entries.sense_en: a large mouthful of drink swallowed at once

synonyms.nuance: Fast and noisy swallow.
Informal; a quick drink from a bottle.

entries.sense_en: promised in marriage

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word.
A noun for the promised man; here betrothed is an adjective.

entries.sense_en: to risk something valuable on the result of a bet

synonyms.nuance: Common; give money on a result.
Allow the chance of losing.
Risk on luck.

entries.sense_en: clothes, especially fine or formal ones

synonyms.nuance: Formal; the clothes for an event.
Special clothes for a role or place.
The plain everyday word.

entries.sense_en: sewn on cloth with a pattern of colored thread

synonyms.nuance: Sewn, but not necessarily a design.
Plain word for joining or decorating with thread.

entries.sense_en: secret help or agreement in something wrong

synonyms.nuance: Secret partnership to cheat others.
Being a partner in a wrong act.

entries.sense_en: a ruler who governs a place in the king's name

synonyms.nuance: Rules a region; may be elected.
Rules when a king is too young or away.

entries.sense_en: the act of betraying someone's trust

synonyms.nuance: Common; also personal.
A crime against one's country.

entries.sense_en: things that serve as proof or a sign of something

synonyms.nuance: Any evidence that shows something is true.
A more general mark or signal.

entries.sense_en: and so; for that reason

synonyms.nuance: Same meaning in modern speech.
Formal; as a result.

entries.sense_en: said to be visited by ghosts or evil spirits

synonyms.nuance: Under a bad spell; not necessarily with ghosts.
Strange and frightening, without ghosts.

entries.sense_en: a male deer

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for a male deer.
Male deer, also rabbit or goat.

entries.tip_ko: heart(심장)와 발음이 거의 같습니다. 철자 hart는 사슴입니다.

entries.sense_en: gone far into a place

synonyms.nuance: Make a hole with something sharp.
Just go in; no sense of difficulty.
Enter secretly.

entries.sense_en: an underground room used for storing or burying things

synonyms.nuance: Below a house, for wine and food.
Under a church, for burials.

entries.sense_en: a thin stick used to do magic

synonyms.nuance: Long and strong stick, often for walking.
A thin stick; more general.

entries.sense_en: a wish or tendency to do something

synonyms.nuance: Stronger and more emotional.
Sudden strong feeling.
A habit rather than a wish.

entries.sense_en: under a magic spell

synonyms.nuance: Under an evil witch's spell.
Full of magic; not necessarily cast under a spell.

entries.sense_en: to catch up with someone or something moving ahead

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrase; the same meaning here. In modern use, overtake often means to go past as well.
Run faster than someone.

entries.sense_en: the wife or husband of a ruler

synonyms.nuance: Any husband or wife.
A woman who rules or is married to a king.

entries.tip_ko: 명사는 첫 음절에 강세가 있습니다: CON-sort.

entries.sense_en: to pretend to be someone else

synonyms.nuance: To copy a person; more formal.
Pretend to be someone in order to trick people.

entries.modern: "pass myself off for him" → "pass myself off as him"

entries.sense_en: to dare to do something risky

synonyms.nuance: Stronger; needs real courage.
Accept a chance of harm.

entries.sense_en: happened to someone, usually something bad

synonyms.nuance: Neutral; any event.
Suddenly reach someone, as a disaster.

entries.sense_en: refused to give way to what others wanted

synonyms.nuance: General; refuse to give in.
Refuse to give up.

entries.modern: "he stood out against them" → "he refused to give in to them"

entries.sense_en: safe from; not harmed by

synonyms.nuance: Cannot be harmed, usually by disease.
Can stand it, though not completely.

entries.sense_en: people who make things by hand as a trade

synonyms.nuance: A skilled maker, often a man.
Any person who has a job.

entries.sense_en: happened; went

synonyms.nuance: Simple word.
Says the final result.

entries.modern: "it fared with him as with his brother" → "it went for him as for his brother"

entries.sense_en: felt very sorry for what he had done

synonyms.nuance: General; wish something had not happened.
Do something to make up for a wrong.
Literary; feel sorrow for something.

entries.sense_en: cried out sadly about a loss

synonyms.nuance: Formal; show deep grief.
Grieve for someone who is dead.
